items.setupText: A repair log says, 'A specialist inspected every instrument.' The intended claim allows different instruments to have different inspectors; it does not identify one specialist who inspected the whole collection.

Every instrument was inspected by a specialist, not necessarily the same one.
Every instrument was inspected by a different specialist from the one who inspected any other instrument.
For every specialist, there was an instrument that the specialist inspected.
items.answer: Every instrument was inspected by a specialist, not necessarily the same one.

items.setupText: To hear him describe the crossing, you would think the sea had been perfectly calm.
items.taskText: Which expansion preserves the opening infinitive's conditional function?
options: You would assume the sea was calm in order to hear his description of the crossing.
Having heard his description of the crossing, you knew the sea had been perfectly calm.
If the sea had been perfectly calm, he would have described the crossing to you.
If you heard his account, you would picture a perfectly calm sea.
items.answer: If you heard his account, you would picture a perfectly calm sea.

items.setupText: The workshop failed not so much because the tools were old as because nobody knew how to use them.
items.taskText: Which editorial comment accurately describes the 'not so much ... as' construction here?
options: It makes the second cause conditional on the first cause having been proved false.
It gives equal causal weight to tool age and lack of training.
It makes lack of know-how the stronger explanation without necessarily excluding tool age as a factor.
It contrasts an early failure caused by old tools with a later failure caused by inexperience.
items.answer: It makes lack of know-how the stronger explanation without necessarily excluding tool age as a factor.
items.explanation: The comparative contrast shifts causal emphasis; it is weaker than a categorical 'not because A but because B' rejection.

items.setupText: 'The pianist said that she would record the sonata in June.' The editor wants 'in June' to date the saying, while leaving the recording date unspecified.
items.taskText: Which revision makes that attachment explicit without asserting that the recording took place?

items.setupText: 'The plumber I thought had cancelled arrived at the flat.' A learner proposes adding 'she' after 'thought' because 'had cancelled' otherwise seems to lack a subject.

The addition makes no structural difference because 'she' is the subject of 'arrived'.

items.setupText: Had the road remained open, we would still have walked, cumbersome though our bags were.
